messages:
maria: FYI we're still seeing ~20–30% of traffic hitting us-west2 even though we flipped Route53 weighted failover to us-east1 22m ago. I just checked the record TTL - it was set to 14400s on a subset of A records. Lowered to 60s ~5m ago but many resolvers still return the old IPs. Any recommended stop-gap?
ajay: can confirm. Healthchecks showed nodepool in us-west2 degraded ~25m ago. We set weight=0 / weight=100 in Route53 and lowered TTL to 60s. Some ISPs still honoring the old 4h TTL.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-18-022 - regional failover (us-west2 -> us-east1) - assigned to @maria and @ajay
ralph: echoing dig from my laptop:```
$ dig +nocmd api.redwood-inference.internal A +noall +answer @1.1.1.1
api.redwood-inference.internal. 13879 IN A 35.201.22.11
```
TTL there is still ~13.8k which matches the old 14400. That answers why traffic is sticky.
maria: ugh. Looks like some resolver chains cached the record before we lowered TTL. We can't force clear remote caches. What are options for traffic shaping while caches expire?
sre-lead: immediate playbook: 1) confirm which resolvers are returning stale IPs (dig @8.8.8.8, @1.1.1.1, major ISP resolvers). 2) For endpoints where we control edges (Cloudflare/Front Door), enable proxying for the domain so traffic funnels through a hop we control and we can route to new region. 3) If proxying isn't an option, update the old IPs to return 302 -> new region endpoint OR return a lightweight 503 with Retry-After to prompt clients to re-resolve. 4) Document exact timestamps for post-incident.
ajay: checked major resolvers: 8.8.8.8 shows TTL 13790, 1.1.1.1 shows TTL 13850, comcast resolver shows TTL still ~13k. Cloudflare public (1.1.1.1) picked up new TTL but still serving old IPs.
ralph: adding the redirect on the old host is low-risk and fast. Can we change the backend on the us-west2 LB to serve a 302 to the us-east1 hostname? That would require updating LB config, but should be quick.
maria: I can patch the us-west2 target group to return 302 -> api-us-east1.redwood-inference.internal. That will route new sessions to the correct region without relying on DNS re-resolve. Doing it now.
dev-platform: note: some clients cache DNS at app level (our mobile SDK has a hard cache for 30m). For those, DNS changes won't help; redirect approach helps only for HTTP clients that follow Location headers. RPC clients may still hard-pin IPs until app-level cache expires.
ajay: good point. For critical RPC flows we should enforce graceful rejection on the old IPs (return error that triggers client to re-resolve) or rotate the cert (too heavy).
ralph: for visibility run this to sample resolver set (paste results here):```
for r in 8.8.8.8 1.1.1.1 9.9.9.9 208.67.222.222; do echo "--- $r"; dig @${r} api.redwood-inference.internal A +short +ttl; done
```
maria: done - pasted in #inc-ops-logs. Also changed us-west2 LB to 302 -> api-us-east1 at 17:41 UTC. Early signs: traffic to us-west2 backend dropped from 28% to 6% in the last 8m.
sre-lead: great. Followups for post-incident: 1) audit Terraform that manages DNS records - make TTL defaults explicit and add a preflight check for TTL > 1h on production failover records. 2) Update runbook to include immediate edge-proxy enablement option. 3) Add a canary step to lower TTL well ahead of planned maintenance (72h prior at least for long TTLs).
ajay: cost note - enabling Cloudflare proxying for the internal domain will add some egress and requests routing cost, but small compared to flapping GPU jobs during failed region. Logging for the redirect will slightly spike.
maria: endpoint telemetry: there were ~4200 connections from IPs that still resolved to old A records between 17:20–17:40. After redirect change it's down to ~950 and falling. We'll keep monitoring.
ops-bot: Update INC-2026-03-18-022 status -> mitigation in place (partial), monitoring.
sre-lead: action items (short): - dev-platform: flag SDK-level DNS caching and add option to respect TTLs or expose forced re-resolve. - infra: add TTL lint rule in CI for DNS terraform. - eng-sre: add step to run resolver sampling script as part of incident checklist.
dev-platform: acked. We can push an SDK patch but that won't help existing clients. We'll add guidance to force reconnect on major incidents.
ralph: small extra note: Route53 supports weighted failover with health checks but that only affects new resolvers; it doesn't clear caches. Also beware of negative caching for NXDOMAIN if we switch names.
maria: agree. Postmortem planned, will include timeline and TTL misconfig details. For now mitigation is working. :thumbsup:
